advisories.summary: envd: Host file disclosure through requirements path traversal and TOCTOU
advisories.description:
### Summary

envd’s `install.python_packages(requirements=...)` could read files outside the build context on the host. Content interpreted as dependency entries could appear in build logs and build-step metadata.

Commit f576c92, released in v1.3.5, added path containment validation but left a time-of-check/time-of-use (TOCTOU) race between symlink resolution and opening the requirements file. Commit 9d575b3 addresses this race by opening requirements files through a directory-rooted filesystem handle.

### Details

envd reads requirements files on the host to determine whether their contents can be embedded directly into a pip installation build step.

The vulnerable host-side requirements read was introduced in v0.3.38. Version v1.3.5 added containment checks for static path escapes but remained vulnerable to a TOCTOU race. The complete fix is included in v1.3.6.

Before f576c92, this host read lacked a build-context containment check. That commit added frontend path validation and a compile-time check using filepath.EvalSymlinks followed by a containment comparison.

However, symlink resolution returns a pathname rather than a pinned filesystem object. The subsequent os.Open independently resolves that pathname. Concurrent filesystem changes could therefore invalidate the containment check before the file was opened.

The complete fix uses os.OpenRoot and Root.Open to enforce containment during filesystem traversal.

Resources:
- first commit: be783264fdd79ad7262cea0485b7d449ca514f80
- Initial containment fix: f576c92
- TOCTOU fix: 9d575b3

### Proof of concept

The security-relevant condition is a requirements-file pathname whose filesystem resolution changes between validation and opening. The containment check describes the filesystem at validation time, while the later pathname-based open may access a different object.

The fix includes a deterministic regression test for the underlying object-pinning guarantee. It opens a context directory handle, moves that directory, and creates a replacement directory at the original pathname containing different requirements. The rooted reader continues reading the original context; a pathname-based reader reads the replacement.

This regression test demonstrates the distinction between rooted and pathname-based reads. It is not an end-to-end demonstration of host file disclosure.

### Impact

An attacker who can influence the build input—and, for the residual race in v1.3.5, concurrently modify the relevant filesystem paths—may cause envd to read files outside the intended build context, subject to the permissions of the envd process.

Depending on the file contents and requirements parsing, information may be exposed through dependency debug logs and build-step metadata. This issue does not establish arbitrary code execution or unrestricted disclosure of every file.

v1.3.5 remains affected by the TOCTOU variant. Earlier versions containing the host requirements-reading behavior are affected by the original containment issue; confirm the earliest affected release before setting the advisory’s version range.

Patched version: v1.3.6.

advisories.summary: rails-html-sanitizer: Possible regular expression denial of service with certain configurations
advisories.description:
## Summary

`Rails::HTML::PermitScrubber` restricts the `href` and `xlink:href` attributes of SVG reference elements to local references. That check matched the attribute value against `/^\s*[^#\s].*/m`. In Ruby `^` anchors to every line start and `\s` matches newlines, so an all-whitespace value made the engine rescan the value from each of its line starts, taking time quadratic in its length.

- Versions affected: `>= 1.0.3, < 1.7.2`
- Not affected: `< 1.0.3`
- Fixed versions: `1.7.2`

Only Ruby 3.1 and earlier are affected. Ruby 3.2 added linear-time regexp matching, which makes the pattern linear.

## Impact

An attacker who supplies HTML to be sanitized can consume CPU out of proportion to the input size, by sending an SVG reference element whose `href` or `xlink:href` is a long run of whitespace.

Applications are affected only when the allowed tags are overridden to include an SVG reference element such as `use`, along with `href` or `xlink:href` in the allowed attributes. The default allowed tags include no SVG elements, so the default configuration is not affected. Applications that use Loofah directly are exposed through its own copy of the check, fixed in Loofah 2.25.3.

## Workarounds

Run Ruby 3.2 or later, which matches the pattern in linear time, or remove the SVG reference elements from the overridden allowed tags.

## Credit

Reported by scyoon through the Rails HackerOne program.

advisories.summary: OpenTelemetry Python API: Denial of service through quadratic-time traceparent parsing
advisories.description:
## Summary

`TraceContextTextMapPropagator.extract()` in `opentelemetry-api` is vulnerable to regular expression denial of service (ReDoS) when processing a specially crafted `traceparent` value.

A malformed value containing a trace-context prefix followed by a long whitespace sequence and an embedded newline triggers quadratic-time regex backtracking. Applications that extract trace context from untrusted carriers accepting such strings can experience excessive CPU consumption and request-processing delays.

When extraction runs on an asynchronous server’s event-loop thread, a single malicious message can delay unrelated requests handled by that event loop.

## Exposure conditions

Exploitation requires attacker-controlled input to reach the affected propagator through a carrier that preserves embedded newlines and permits a sufficiently large value.

Conforming HTTP header values cannot contain embedded newlines. However, OpenTelemetry carriers are not restricted to HTTP headers. JSON strings can contain escaped newlines that become newline characters after decoding.

MCP request metadata is one relevant integration path: applications may extract trace context from JSON `params._meta`. Exposure depends on the MCP SDK or instrumentation version, whether extraction invokes the W3C Trace Context propagator, and applicable message-size limits. HTTP header validation does not constrain a `traceparent` string carried inside a JSON body.

Authentication requirements depend on the application exposing the carrier.

## Impact

The demonstrated impact is denial of service through excessive CPU consumption and blocked request processing. Repeated malicious messages may sustain service degradation.

This finding does not demonstrate data disclosure, data modification, or code execution.

## Remediation

Upgrade `opentelemetry-api` to `1.45.2` or a later release containing the fix.

Version `1.45.2` rejects `traceparent` values longer than 512 characters before regex matching and removes the overlapping suffix and trailing-whitespace expressions.

Where upgrading is temporarily unavailable, reject oversized values and embedded CR/LF characters before passing untrusted trace-context values to the affected propagator.

advisories.summary: Soup Sieve: Exponential ReDoS in selector compilation via \9-run in CSS_ESCAPES/IDENTIFIER
advisories.description:
### Summary
The IDENTIFIER/CSS_ESCAPES regex (css_parser.py:119-124) exhibits exponential backtracking on a run of ambiguous digit-escapes (`\9`) in an attribute-name or tag position of an otherwise well-formed selector. It fires at compile time (before the SELECTOR_LIMIT guard) via the public `soupsieve.compile()` and BeautifulSoup `.select()`.

### PoC (verified on soupsieve 2.9.2)

    import soupsieve as sv
    sv.compile('[a' + '\\9'*26 + '=x]')   # ~57 bytes -> ~10s; ~16x time per +4 chars

### Novelty
Distinct from the patched GHSA-836r-... (VALUE regex) and GHSA-2wc2-... (comma-list) advisories, which are fixed in 2.9.2; this is a different regex/vector.

### Reachability
CSS selectors are usually developer-controlled, so exposure requires an application that compiles UNTRUSTED selector strings (web-scraping-as-a-service, no-code/query builders, user-defined extraction rules). Where selectors are user-supplied, a ~60-byte string hangs the worker.

### Note
This issue was fixed in version 3.0.0, which has been yanked from the PyPI registry. Use versions 3.0.2 and above to upgrade.

advisories.summary: Soup Sieve: Uncontrolled recursion in CSS parser lets nested pseudo-class selectors exhaust the Python call stack
advisories.description:
## Summary

The Soup Sieve CSS selector parser recurses once per level of nested pseudo-class selector (`:is()`, `:not()`, `:where()`, `:has()`) without any limit on nesting depth. An unauthenticated attacker who can supply a CSS selector string to `soupsieve.compile()`, `soupsieve.select()`, or Beautiful Soup's `soup.select()` / `soup.select_one()` can force the parser to exceed Python's recursion limit with a small crafted input (about 1.6 KB, roughly 330 nesting levels), raising an uncontrolled `RecursionError`. Because this exception is not part of the parser's documented error contract, applications that catch only `ValueError` or `SelectorSyntaxError` see an unexpected failure of the request or task that parsed the selector.

## Root Cause

The parser dispatches each opening pseudo-class token to `parse_pseudo_open`, which calls back into `parse_selectors` to parse the pseudo-class body. Every nesting level therefore adds Python stack frames, and no counter, depth guard, or `RecursionError` handler bounds this descent. The token-count guard `SELECTOR_LIMIT = 8192` (added for the earlier comma-separated-list memory issue) counts parsed tokens, not recursion depth; at the failing nesting depth the token count is only about 330, roughly four percent of that limit, so the guard never fires. The security invariant that untrusted selector input must not be able to exhaust interpreter resources is not enforced for nesting depth.

```text
soupsieve/css_parser.py
  CSSParser.parse_pseudo_open (line 985): sel.selectors.append(self.parse_selectors(iselector, index, flags))
  CSSParser.parse_selectors  (line 1137): recursive target; dispatches pseudo-class tokens back into parse_pseudo_class -> parse_pseudo_open
  CSSParser.increment_count  (lines 707-712): SELECTOR_LIMIT token guard; increments once per nesting level, cannot bound depth
```

## Impact

Any application that compiles or evaluates untrusted CSS selectors through Soup Sieve (directly or via Beautiful Soup) is affected. No authentication, privilege, or user interaction is required; the failure occurs during selector parsing, before any document is matched. A single crafted selector of about 1.6 KB reliably raises `RecursionError`. The demonstrated capability is a transient denial of the individual request, task, or invocation that parsed the malicious selector: the exception propagates uncaught unless the caller handles `RecursionError` (or a broad `except Exception`). The `RecursionError` in CPython 3.x is a recoverable stack unwind, not an interpreter crash or persistent resource exhaustion, and it carries no confidentiality or integrity impact. Applications following the parser's documented error pattern (catching `ValueError` / `SelectorSyntaxError`) will not catch it, so a repeated stream of such selectors can plausibly cause repeated per-request failures; this per-request availability effect is the demonstrated consequence, not a service-wide or amplified outage.

## Proof of Concept

Requires only an installed Soup Sieve (any release from 0.4 through 2.10) and a default CPython recursion limit of 1000. No Beautiful Soup document or network setup is needed.

```python
import soupsieve as sv

# ~330 levels of nested :is() around a single tag: about 1.6 KB of input.
depth = 330
selector = ":is(" * depth + "a" + ")" * depth
print("selector length:", len(selector))
sv.compile(selector)
```

```text
selector length: 1651
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
  File ".../soupsieve/css_parser.py", line 985, in parse_pseudo_open
    sel.selectors.append(self.parse_selectors(iselector, index, flags))
RecursionError: maximum recursion depth exceeded
```

The same failure was reproduced with `:not()`, `:where()`, and `:has()`, and through `BeautifulSoup(...).select(selector)`. A negative control at depth 100 compiles successfully with a token count of 101, confirming the token guard is far from firing.

## Attack Chain

1. **Exposure:** The application exposes `soupsieve.compile()` / `select()` or Beautiful Soup's `.select()` / `.select_one()` to attacker-influenced CSS selector input. These are the library's primary public API and ship enabled by default; Soup Sieve is an automatic dependency of Beautiful Soup 4.
2. **Control:** The attacker fully controls the selector string. The nested pseudo-class pattern (`:is(:is(...a...))`) survives tokenization and normalization unchanged.
3. **Path:** `compile()` reaches `CSSParser.process_selectors()` and then `parse_selectors()`, which dispatches each pseudo-class token through `parse_pseudo_class()` into `parse_pseudo_open()`, which calls `parse_selectors()` again, once per nesting level.
4. **Guard:** The only resource guard is the `SELECTOR_LIMIT` token counter, which reaches about 330 at the failing depth versus its limit of 8192, so it never fires. No recursion-depth counter and no `RecursionError` handler exist anywhere in the package.
5. **Primitive:** Python's recursion limit is exceeded during parsing, raising an uncontrolled `RecursionError`.
6. **Result:** The unhandled `RecursionError` propagates to the caller, failing the request, task, or process invocation that parsed the selector, outside the parser's documented `ValueError` / `SelectorSyntaxError` error contract.

## Bypass Evidence

The relevant existing guard is the `SELECTOR_LIMIT = 8192` token counter in `increment_count()`. It does not block this path: it increments once per nesting level, so at the failing depth of about 330 the count is roughly 330 (about four percent of 8192), verified by instrumenting `increment_count` and observing a maximum count of 329 at the point `RecursionError` was raised. A search of the package for `RecursionError` and `RuntimeError` handlers returns no matches, so nothing catches the error internally, and `functools.lru_cache` on the compile path does not cache exceptions. Attempts to invalidate the finding were made and failed: raising the interpreter recursion limit only shifts the required nesting depth (a proportionally larger but still small selector), and a broad `except Exception` in the caller does catch the error but the parser's documented contract raises only `ValueError` / `SelectorSyntaxError`, so callers coded to that contract remain exposed. This is a distinct weakness from the prior comma-separated-list memory-exhaustion advisory: that issue exhausts heap memory through linear object expansion and was addressed by the token count limit, whereas this issue exhausts the call stack through unbounded recursion depth and is not addressed by any released version, including 2.8.4 which was independently confirmed to still raise `RecursionError` on this input.

## Affected Versions

- `Ecosystem: pip (PyPI)`
- `Package: soupsieve`
- `Confirmed affected range: >= 0.4, <= 2.10`
- `Latest release checked: soupsieve 2.10 (PyPI, latest published release as of 2026-09-25)`
- `Fix status: not fixed in any released version`

The recursive `parse_pseudo_open` to `parse_selectors` structure is present in the earliest PyPI release (0.4) and in every subsequent release through the current 2.10, verified against the published PyPI source artifacts. Version 2.5, release 2.8.4 (which added that token-count limit), and 2.10 were each executed and confirmed to raise `RecursionError` on the crafted input. No released version adds a recursion-depth limit; the token-count `SELECTOR_LIMIT` introduced in 2.8.4 is architecturally unable to bound nesting depth. There is no registry or tag disagreement and no package or module path change.

## Possible Solution

Python's `RecursionError` is sometimes a contested issue related to security. The Soup Sieve project does not consider it "uncontrolled" and allows it to be raised to indicate Python's maximum recursion depth was reached, and allows it to fail to prevent overflows, a much worse and real security vulnerability. With that said, the algorithm can be reworked to be non-recursive, allowing the selector limit check to now capture and raise an exception. In addition, the limit could be exposed to the user to give them better control.

## Mitigation

For those on older versions where the algorithm is still recursive, a try/except block that captures `RecursionError` can be added around calls if accepting untrusted user input is allowed.

## Note

This issue was fixed in version 3.0.0, which has been yanked from the PyPI registry. Use versions 3.0.2 and above to upgrade.

---

Reported by zx (GitHub: @manus-pi).

advisories.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

posix-cpu-timers: Prevent...
advisories.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

posix-cpu-timers: Prevent UAF caused by non-leader exec() race

Wongi and Jungwoo decoded and reported a non-leader exec() related race
which can result in an UAF:

 sys_timer_delete()			exec()
   posix_cpu_timer_del()
   // Observes old leader
   p = pid_task(pid, pid_type);		de_thread()
   					  switch_leader();
					  release_task(old_leader)
					    __exit_signal(old_leader)
					      sighand = lock(old_leader, sighand);
					      posix_cpu_timers*_exit();
   sighand = lock_task_sighand(p)	      unhash_task(old_leader);
     sh = lock(p, sighand)	    	      old_leader->sighand = NULL;
					      unlock(sighand);
     (p->sighand == NULL)
	unlock(sh)
	return NULL;

   // Returns without action
   if(!sighand)
      return 0;
   free_posix_timer();

This is "harmless" unless the deleted timer was armed and enqueued in
p->signal because on exec() a TGID targeted timer is inherited.

As sys_timer_delete() freed the underlying posix timer object
run_posix_cpu_timers() or any timerqueue related add/delete operations on
other timers will access the freed object's timerqueue node, which results
in an UAF.

There is a similar problem vs. posix_cpu_timer_set(). For regular posix
timers it just transiently returns -ESRCH to user space, but for the use
case in do_cpu_nanosleep() it's the same UAF just that the k_itimer is
allocated on the stack.

Also posix_cpu_timer_rearm() fails to rearm the timer, which means it stops
to expire.

While debating solutions Frederic pointed out another problem:

   posix_cpu_timer_del(tmr)
					__exit_signal(p)
					  posix_cpu_timers*_exit(p);
					  unhash_task(p);
					  p->sighand = NULL;
     sh = lock_task_sighand(p)
        sighand = p->sighand;
	if (!sighand)
	    return NULL;
	lock(sighand);

     if (!sh)
	WARN_ON_ONCE(timer_queued(tmr));

On weakly ordered architectures it is not guaranteed that
posix_cpu_timer_del() will observe the stores in posix_cpu_timers*_exit()
when p->sighand is observed as NULL, which means the WARN() can be a false
positive.

Solve these issues by:

  1) Changing the store in __exit_signal() to smp_store_release().

  2) Adding a smp_acquire__after_ctrl_dep() into the !sighand path
     of lock_task_sighand().

  3) Creating a helper function for looking up the task and locking sighand
     which does not return when sighand == NULL. Instead it retries the
     task lookup and only if that fails it gives up.

  4) Using that helper in the three affected functions.

#1/#2 ensures that the reader side which observes sighand == NULL also
observes all preceeding stores, i.e. the stores in posix_cpu_timers*_exit()
and the ones in unhash_task().

#3 ensures that the above described non-leader exec() situation is handled
gracefully. When the task lookup returns the old leader, but sighand ==
NULL then it retries. In the non-leader exec() case the subsequent task
lookup will observe the new leader due to #1/#2. In normal exit() scenarios
the subsequent lookup fails.

When the task lookup fails, the function also checks whether the timer is
still enqueued and issues a warning if that's the case. Unfortunately there
is nothing which can be done about it, but as the task is already not
longer visible the timer should not be accessed anymore. This check also
requires memory ordering, which is not provided when the first lookup
fails. To achieve that the check is preceeded by a smp_rmb() which pairs
with the smp_wmb() in write_seqlock() in __exit_signal(). That ensures that
the stores in posix_cpu_timers*_exit() are visible.

The history of the non-leader exec() issue goes back to the early days of
posix CPU timers, which stored a pointer to the group leader task in the
timer. That obviously fails when a non-leader exec() switches the leader.

advisories.summary: In Eclipse BaSyx Go Components versions up to and including 1.1.3, ABAC-enabled deployments match...
advisories.description:
In Eclipse BaSyx Go Components versions up to and including 1.1.3, ABAC-enabled deployments match `ROUTE` access rules against the fully decoded request path, while the router routes on the raw, still encoded path. An encoded slash (`%2F`) inside a path value is a segment separator for the access check but part of the value for the router, so a request can match a narrow `ROUTE` rule while the handler returns a different, larger resource.



An authenticated caller whose rules grant READ only on parts of a resource can therefore read the whole resource. In the DPP API, a rule such as `/v1/dpps/*/elements/*`, meant to grant only passport elements, also grants the complete passport whose identifier contains `/elements/`. In the Submodel Repository, AAS Repository and AAS Environment, a rule such as `/submodels/*/submodel-elements/*/attachment`, meant to grant only file attachments, also grants the complete element whose stored idShort contains `%2F`.



The issue is fixed in Eclipse BaSyx Go Components v1.1.4.

advisories.summary: A flaw was found in Foreman’s Api::V2::PersonalAccessTokensController, where Foreman::Controller:...

Additionally, the POST and PUT /api/v2/users/:user_id/mail_notifications paths call deny_access when the requester is unauthorized but fail to halt execution, allowing the request to continue and persist the unauthorized change despite a 403 response or subsequent DoubleRenderError. This can allow a user to disclose another user’s mail-notification configuration, including mail_query values, and, where write permissions apply, modify or create notification settings for another user.

advisories.summary: Omnispace Agora Project before 26.10.0 contains a vulnerability where the persistent remember-me...
advisories.description: Omnispace Agora Project before 26.10.0 contains a vulnerability where the persistent remember-me token is stored verbatim server-side, making the stored value identical to the bearer credential held in the user's cookie. Attackers who gain access to the stored token, such as through database or backup disclosure, can replay the plaintext value to authenticate as the victim user without needing their password.

advisories.summary: A flaw was found in sequoia-openpgp. The library incorrectly infers key flags for older...
advisories.description: A flaw was found in sequoia-openpgp. The library incorrectly infers key flags for older certificates when a key flags subpacket is missing, leading to a discrepancy in how key capabilities are viewed. This key flag confusion allows an attacker to bypass the back-signature check. Consequently, an attacker can illegitimately bind an arbitrary subkey to their own certificate and forge signatures, completely compromising cryptographic integrity.

advisories.summary: Omnispace Agora Project before 26.10.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that...
advisories.description: Omnispace Agora Project before 26.10.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated users to inject malicious script by uploading a file with HTML/script markup embedded in its filename, which bypasses the paramFilter since uploaded-file names arrive through $_FILES rather than $_GET/$_POST. Attackers can upload a file with a crafted name such as an SVG onload payload to have the unsanitized filename stored and later rendered to other users, resulting in script execution in their browsers.

advisories.summary: A flaw was found in Candlepin. The central authorization filter incorrectly grants access when...
advisories.description: A flaw was found in Candlepin. The central authorization filter incorrectly grants access when any one of multiple @Verify-annotated parameters is accessible, instead of requiring access to every verified entity. A low-privilege authenticated attacker who can access the first referenced object can bypass authorization checks on subsequent objects. When target resource identifiers are known, this can enable unauthorized disclosure of consumer information and unauthorized modification of entitlements and related subscription resources, including across organizations.

advisories.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

bpf, sockmap: reject...
advisories.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

bpf, sockmap: reject overflowing copy + len in bpf_msg_push_data()

When the scatterlist ring is full or nearly full, bpf_msg_push_data()
enters a copy fallback path and computes copy + len for the page
allocation size. Since len comes from BPF with arg3_type = ARG_ANYTHING
and both are u32, a crafted len can wrap the sum to a small value,
causing an undersized allocation followed by an out-of-bounds memcpy.

 BUG: unable to handle page fault for address: ffffed104089a402
 Oops: Oops: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN NOPTI
 Call Trace:
  __asan_memcpy (mm/kasan/shadow.c:105)
  bpf_msg_push_data (net/core/filter.c:2852 net/core/filter.c:2788)
  bpf_prog_9ed8b5711920a7d7+0x2e/0x36
  sk_psock_msg_verdict (net/core/skmsg.c:934)
  tcp_bpf_sendmsg (net/ipv4/tcp_bpf.c:421 net/ipv4/tcp_bpf.c:584)
  __sys_sendto (net/socket.c:2206)
  do_syscall_64 (arch/x86/entry/syscall_64.c:94)
  entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe (arch/x86/entry/entry_64.S:130)

Add an overflow check before the allocation.

advisories.summary: The Yoast SEO – Advanced SEO with real-time guidance and built-in AI plugin for WordPress is...
advisories.description: The Yoast SEO – Advanced SEO with real-time guidance and built-in AI plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Post Slug (post_name) in all versions up to, and including, 28.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with author-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires pretty permalinks to be enabled, as the exploit chain depends on get_permalink() embedding the stored percent-encoded post_name in the generated URL.

advisories.summary: XWEB EVO 4.3.0 through 5.8.8 contains an unauthenticated arbitrary file write vulnerability that...
advisories.description: XWEB EVO 4.3.0 through 5.8.8 contains an unauthenticated arbitrary file write vulnerability that allows remote attackers to modify the system configuration file /etc/xwebconfig.json by sending a crafted POST request to config.lua with action=set, which performs no session validation and writes the raw, unvalidated request body. Attackers can tamper with configuration values such as model and plugin fields or trigger a SYSTEM_NOT_CONFIGURED state via the unauthenticated action=get and action=set operations, resulting in configuration tampering and denial of service. This product line reached it's end of service date in March 2026.

advisories.summary: XWEB EVO 5.6.2 through 5.8.8 contains a hardcoded credential vulnerability where the...
advisories.description: XWEB EVO 5.6.2 through 5.8.8 contains a hardcoded credential vulnerability where the Administrator web account is configured to use password_mode daily_password with no stored password, as the Users.authenticate function in lualib_users.lua synthesizes the Administrator configuration without validating any stored secret. Attackers who can derive the MAC-based daily password can authenticate as Administrator to obtain a full admin session on the device. This product line reached it's end of service date in March 2026.

advisories.summary: XWEB EVO 5.2.3 through 5.8.8 contains an authenticated OS command injection vulnerability that...
advisories.description: XWEB EVO 5.2.3 through 5.8.8 contains an authenticated OS command injection vulnerability that allows authenticated attackers to execute arbitrary commands as root by injecting shell metacharacters into the output device path parameter processed by backup.lua. Attackers can exploit the unescaped concatenation into mount, unzip, and related shell commands run via the wlua interpreter, including through the setuid xwbackup.cgi and xwrestore.cgi interfaces, to achieve full system compromise. This product line reached it's end of service date in March 2026.

advisories.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

inet: reject unhashed...
advisories.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

inet: reject unhashed sockets during established lookups

TCP established ehash lookups are lockless. The socket caches involved
use SLAB_TYPESAFE_BY_RCU, so memory can be reused before an RCU reader
that retained its old address has finished.

After a tuple match, __inet_lookup_established() and
__inet6_lookup_established() acquire a reference and repeat the tuple
check. They do not check whether the new object is hashed. If the
address is reused for a socket with the same tuple, the lookup can
acquire a reference to the new object and return it while its nulls node
is unhashed.

A PoC that drives reuse with a SYN cookie request socket reproduced the
crash. The new request socket is unhashed and has a NULL rsk_listener.
A lookup that had loaded the address of the old request socket acquired
the reference published by tcp_get_cookie_sock() and returned the new
object. tcp_v4_rcv() then read sk_state through the NULL listener.

The resulting crash was:

  BUG: kernel NULL pointer dereference, address: 0000000000000012
  #PF: supervisor read access in kernel mode
  #PF: error_code(0x0000) - not-present page
  ...
  Oops: Oops: 0000 [#1] SMP NOPTI
  CPU: 4 UID: 0 PID: 0 Comm: swapper/4 Not tainted 7.3.0-00591-g0e135910deec #1 PREEMPT(lazy)
  ...
  RIP: 0010:tcp_v4_rcv+0x44e/0x1280
  ...
  R10: 0000000000000001 R11: 00000000024ca8c0 R12: 0000000000000000
  ...
  CR2: 0000000000000012 CR3: 0000000103d50004 CR4: 0000000000770ef0
  ...
  Call Trace:
   <IRQ>
   ? raw_local_deliver+0xae/0x240
   ip_protocol_deliver_rcu+0x2d/0x180
   ip_local_deliver_finish+0x84/0x100
   ip_sublist_rcv_finish+0x5f/0x70
   ip_sublist_rcv+0x12a/0x1d0
   ip_list_rcv+0xfd/0x130
   __netif_receive_skb_list_core+0x223/0x250
   netif_receive_skb_list_internal+0x1d2/0x2c0
   ? try_fill_recv+0x39/0x7b0
   napi_complete_done+0x74/0x170
   virtnet_poll+0x445/0x600
   __napi_poll+0x27/0x1e0
   net_rx_action+0x2fe/0x3b0
   handle_softirqs+0xc2/0x2c0
   __irq_exit_rcu+0x74/0xd0
   common_interrupt+0x7f/0x90
   </IRQ>
  ...
  Kernel panic - not syncing: Fatal exception in interrupt

After taking a reference, check whether the nulls node is unhashed in
both IPv4 and IPv6 established lookups. If it is unhashed or the tuple
no longer matches, drop the reference and restart the lookup.

Lookups racing with the TIME_WAIT hashdance, or with a request being
replaced by its child, now restart and find the new socket instead of
returning the old one.

Request sockets that were never inserted into ehash can have a nonzero
refcount, and a stale lookup can hold a transient reference. Therefore,
when SYN cookie, Fast Open, and request migration paths fail after
setting a nonzero refcount, release the references held by those paths
with reqsk_put() instead of freeing the request directly.

advisories.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xen-netback: Fix UAF when...
advisories.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xen-netback: Fix UAF when reading statistics data

The network statistic data in the driver is protected by RCU.
Unfortunately when tearing down the queues after an error during
connecting to the frontend (e.g. due to illegal Xenstore data filled
in by the guest), the statistic data is being freed without
synchronizing the RCU state.  In case the data is being read via sysfs
in this phase, access to already freed memory or memory being in new
use is possible.

Fix that by calling synchronize_net() before freeing the queue data.

This is XSA-526 / CVE-2026-100080

advisories.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xen-blkback: Avoid UAF when...
advisories.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xen-blkback: Avoid UAF when reading I/O statistics

Reading I/O statistics via sysfs concurrently with tearing down a
frontend device might result in UAF or a NULL dereference, as the
reading of the statistics data is not synchronized with freeing the
data.

Use a rwlock for synchronizing.

This is XSA-528 / CVE-2026-100082

advisories.summary: A flaw was found in the default seccomp profile used by Podman via containers-common. Deny rules...
advisories.description: A flaw was found in the default seccomp profile used by Podman via containers-common. Deny rules for AF_VSOCK and NETLINK_AUDIT compared socket arguments with unmasked 64-bit equality. Because the kernel truncates those int arguments to 32 bits, setting upper bits can bypass the deny rules.

advisories.description: A flaw was found in gcc. An attacker could cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by passing a string that is not null-terminated to the std::from_chars() function in the libstdc++ library. This issue triggers an out-of-bounds read beyond the allocated buffer, potentially leading to invalid data parsing or an application crash.

advisories.description: A flaw was found in libmodulemd. In builds with rpmio support enabled, compressed modulemd YAML is decompressed through a custom read handler that does not enforce a cumulative decompressed-size limit before parsing. An attacker who can supply a highly compressible compressed YAML file can cause excessive CPU and memory consumption, resulting in a denial of service.

advisories.summary: A flaw was found in libmodulemd. In the module stream v2 rpm-map emission path, an inner loop...
advisories.description: A flaw was found in libmodulemd. In the module stream v2 rpm-map emission path, an inner loop incorrectly uses the count of digest algorithms as its bound instead of the number of checksums in the current digest table. Crafted modulemd v2 metadata with multiple digest types can trigger an out-of-bounds read during YAML serialization, typically causing a crash and resulting in a denial of service.

advisories.summary: The `insights-operator-gather` ClusterRole grants the operator's service account read access to...
advisories.description:
The `insights-operator-gather` ClusterRole grants the operator's service account read access to secrets in the core API group with no namespace or resourceNames restriction — therefore, access to every secret in every namespace in the cluster.

Ref: https://github.com/openshift/insights-operator/blob/8f15e3157ff09f54ab22801f5b21da35a195cc6d/manifests/03-clusterrole.yaml#L368-L373
```
- apiGroups:
  - ""
  resources:
  - secrets
  verbs:
  - get
  - list
```

By spawning a pod with the gather service account mounted, an attacker will be able to access any secret in any namespace.

```
spec:
 serviceAccountName:"gather"
```

A remote attacker can exploit this vulnerability by enticing a user to follow a specially crafted link, resulting in the user being redirected to an arbitrary external website after authenticating. This open redirect can be leveraged to conduct phishing attacks or credential theft.

advisories.summary: A heap-based buffer overflow flaw was found in rpm. RPMTAG_FILESIGNATURES in a crafted, unsigned...
advisories.description: A heap-based buffer overflow flaw was found in rpm. RPMTAG_FILESIGNATURES in a crafted, unsigned RPM package's main header is declared with the wrong header type, causing hex2binv() to allocate a one-byte buffer and then write the tag's attacker-controlled, hex-decoded content — of attacker-chosen length — past the end of that allocation. This is reachable via rpm2cpio, rpm2archive, and rpm -qlvp on an untrusted package.

advisories.summary: A flaw was found in flightctl. The configureRepoHTTPSClient() function in the device-render...
advisories.description:
A flaw was found in flightctl. The configureRepoHTTPSClient() function in the device-render worker builds a per-repository tls.Config (which may include InsecureSkipVerify, a custom CA bundle, or tenant-supplied mTLS client certificates) and installs it into go-git's process-global client.Protocols map via gitclient.InstallProtocol("https", ...). Because the worker renders devices for multiple organizations concurrently from a shared goroutine pool, whichever tenant's repository configuration is written last wins for all in-flight git.Clone calls. 
This race condition can cause one tenant's TLS settings, including InsecureSkipVerify or mTLS client credentials, to leak into another tenant's git operations.

advisories.summary: A flaw was found in openshift/oauth-server. The OAuth login and error page endpoints pass the...
advisories.description: A flaw was found in openshift/oauth-server. The OAuth login and error page endpoints pass the unauthenticated Accept-Language header to golang.org/x/text/language.ParseAcceptLanguage() without input validation. A bypass of the CVE-2022-32149 mitigation exists: the upstream guard counts only '-' characters but the internal BCP 47 scanner aliases '_' to '-' after the guard check. An unauthenticated attacker can send a crafted Accept-Language header using '_' separators to trigger quadratic-time parsing, consuming excessive CPU and denying authentication to all cluster users.

advisories.summary:
A flaw was found in GDB's STABS debug format parser. The
read_member_functions() function in gdb...
advisories.description:
A flaw was found in GDB's STABS debug format parser. The
read_member_functions() function in gdb/stabsread.c contains a linked
list removal bug in the code that separates destructor and non-destructor
member functions of C++ classes. The bug causes the destructor entries to
remain in the main function list while the list length counter is
decremented, resulting in an out-of-bounds write when the function list
is copied to its final allocated array. An attacker can craft an ELF
binary with malicious .stab and .stabstr sections that triggers this
out-of-bounds write when a user opens the file in GDB and performs any
symbol-inspection operation such as setting a breakpoint. The inferior
process does not need to be executed. Under controlled conditions, this
was demonstrated to achieve execution of arbitrary commands within the
GDB process.

advisories.summary: A flaw was found in the libstdc++ component of GCC. An attacker who can provide an excessively...
advisories.description: A flaw was found in the libstdc++ component of GCC. An attacker who can provide an excessively large element count to a boolean vector (std::vector<bool>) constructor can trigger an integer wrap during internal memory calculations. This issue leaves the container in an inconsistent state, leading to out-of-bounds memory access and resulting in an application crash or a Denial of Service (DoS) during subsequent operations.

advisories.summary: A flaw was found in libmodulemd. When parsing module metadata, the xmd field is converted into...
advisories.description: A flaw was found in libmodulemd. When parsing module metadata, the xmd field is converted into nested GVariant values through recursive YAML mapping and sequence helpers without a recursion-depth or node-count limit. An attacker who can supply crafted modulemd YAML with deeply nested xmd content can cause stack exhaustion or excessive resource consumption, resulting in a denial of service.

advisories.summary: A flaw was found in the OpenShift console. An authenticated console user can exploit a Server...
advisories.description: A flaw was found in the OpenShift console. An authenticated console user can exploit a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability by providing a specially crafted Helm chart URL without proper validation. This allows the user to make the console pod fetch arbitrary URLs, potentially leading to the disclosure of sensitive information through error messages or enabling blind port scanning within the cluster.

advisories.summary: A heap-based buffer overflow flaw was found in rpm. Parsing a symlink entry in an untrusted RPM...
advisories.description: A heap-based buffer overflow flaw was found in rpm. Parsing a symlink entry in an untrusted RPM package whose declared RPMTAG_LONGFILESIZES value is 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF causes an integer overflow in iterReadArchiveNext() that shrinks a buffer allocation to one byte, after which the payload's independently-controlled cpio filesize field is used to write attacker-controlled data past the end of that allocation. This is reachable via rpm2cpio, rpm2archive, and rpm -qlvp on an  untrusted package.

advisories.summary: Psono Server Community Edition versions 1.12.6 through 7.5.0 and Psono Server Enterprise Edition...
advisories.description: Psono Server Community Edition versions 1.12.6 through 7.5.0 and Psono Server Enterprise Edition before 7.5.1 do not require accepted group membership when authorizing deletion of group share-rights. The DELETE /share/right/ endpoint checks for a membership matching the target group, the authenticated user, and share_admin=True, but omits accepted=True. An authenticated remote attacker who has been invited to a group with share-admin privileges, and who knows a group share-right UUID, can therefore delete that group's share-right record without accepting the invitation or after declining it. Pending invitations have accepted=None, while declined invitations retain accepted=False and the share_admin flag. Deletion revokes the group's access to the affected share and its contained secrets for all accepted group members, without deleting the underlying data or disclosing secret contents. The issue was fixed in version 7.5.1 of both editions, released on 2026-10-13.

advisories.summary: Missing authentication for a critical function (CWE-306) in the management service ...
advisories.description:
Missing authentication for a critical function (CWE-306) in the management service (uavmonitor_usbv1) of the 1300 communications board in DJI AeroScope Mobile (TP703) firmware 03.00.00.26, with 1300 communications board firmware 02.00.07.12 through 02.00.08.40, allows an unauthenticated attacker on the local network to read device information, such as the serial number, MAC address, IP address and radio configuration, and to change configuration settings. The service accepts commands in DJI's proprietary DUML protocol without any authentication. Exploitation requires network access to TCP port 16000 on the board and that the unit is not connected to another controlling host. The same commands are also accepted over the USB operator port. Confirmed on a physical device.



NOTE: This vulnerability only affects products that are no longer supported by the maintainer. DJI has discontinued AeroScope Mobile and no fixed firmware is available.

advisories.summary: Improper verification of cryptographic signature (CWE-347) in the firmware update handler of the...
advisories.description:
Improper verification of cryptographic signature (CWE-347) in the firmware update handler of the management service (uavmonitor_usbv1) of the 1300 communications board in DJI AeroScope Mobile (TP703) firmware 03.00.00.26, with 1300 communications board firmware 02.00.07.12 through 02.00.08.40, allows an unauthenticated attacker on the local network to install modified firmware, which gives persistent code execution as root. The device accepts any image that matches an MD5 checksum supplied in the same request and does not verify a signature. Exploitation requires network access to TCP port 16000 on the board and that the unit is not connected to another controlling host. Reproduced by running the unmodified device binaries in emulation; not tested on a physical device.



NOTE: This vulnerability only affects products that are no longer supported by the maintainer. DJI has discontinued AeroScope Mobile and no fixed firmware is available.

advisories.summary: Use of hard-coded credentials (CWE-798) on the 1300 communications board in DJI AeroScope Mobile ...
advisories.description:
Use of hard-coded credentials (CWE-798) on the 1300 communications board in DJI AeroScope Mobile (TP703) firmware 03.00.00.26, with 1300 communications board firmware 02.00.07.12 through 02.00.08.40, allows an attacker with physical access to the board's serial console to log in as root. The same password hash is present on every unit and uses DES crypt, so the password can be recovered offline from the distributed firmware. No network login service accepts this password by default. Confirmed on a physical device.



NOTE: This vulnerability only affects products that are no longer supported by the maintainer. DJI has discontinued AeroScope Mobile and no fixed firmware is available.

advisories.summary: In Eclipse BaSyx Go Components versions up to and including 1.1.2, ABAC-enabled deployments of...
advisories.description:
In Eclipse BaSyx Go Components versions up to and including 1.1.2, ABAC-enabled deployments of the Submodel Repository and the AAS Environment return Submodel Elements that the caller is not authorized to read from `GET /submodels/{submodelIdentifier}/submodel-elements`.



If an access rule grants READ on a single Submodel Element through a `$sme` `REFERABLE` object, the list route returns every element of that Submodel, including its value, as soon as one element matches the caller's rules. The single-element route and the full Submodel read enforce the same rule and deny access to the other elements. An authenticated caller with a READ grant for one element of a Submodel can therefore read all other elements of that Submodel.



The issue is fixed in Eclipse BaSyx Go Components v1.1.3.

advisories.summary: In Eclipse AAS4J before 3.0.1, `XmlSchemaValidator.validateSchema()` (and `AASXValidator...
advisories.description:
In Eclipse AAS4J before 3.0.1, `XmlSchemaValidator.validateSchema()` (and `AASXValidator.validateSchema()`, which calls it) validates untrusted XML with a default JAXP `Validator` that resolves external DTDs and external entities. An attacker who supplies a crafted AAS XML document or AASX package can read local files from the host, send their contents out-of-band to an attacker-controlled server, and make the validating process send arbitrary outbound requests (SSRF). Validation still returns no errors.



Details:



- Vulnerable code: `dataformat-xml/src/main/java/org/eclipse/digitaltwin/aas4j/v3/dataformat/xml/XmlSchemaValidator.java`. `schema.newValidator().validate(new StreamSource(...))` runs without `ACCESS_EXTERNAL_DTD` / `ACCESS_EXTERNAL_SCHEMA` restrictions and without `disallow-doctype-decl`.



- Second entry point: `dataformat-aasx/src/main/java/org/eclipse/digitaltwin/aas4j/v3/dataformat/aasx/AASXValidator.java`. The AAS XML part of an `.aasx` package is passed unchanged to the vulnerable validator.



- `XmlDeserializer` (Jackson/Woodstox) is not affected, because DTD support is disabled by default there.



- Present since the initial import of the code base (commit `cc9da52`).



- Fix: harden the validator by setting `ACCESS_EXTERNAL_DTD` and `ACCESS_EXTERNAL_SCHEMA` to `""` and rejecting `DOCTYPE` declarations. The bundled `AAS.xsd` does not need DTDs, so no functionality is lost.

advisories.summary: In Eclipse BaSyx Go Components versions up to and including 1.1.2, ABAC-enabled deployments of...
advisories.description:
In Eclipse BaSyx Go Components versions up to and including 1.1.2, ABAC-enabled deployments of the Submodel Repository and the AAS Environment do not apply an access rule's `FILTERLIST` fragment filters to single Submodel reads.



`GET /submodels` removes the fields that a rule's `FILTERLIST` hides, but `GET /submodels/{submodelIdentifier}` and `GET /submodels/{submodelIdentifier}/$metadata` return them unfiltered. An authenticated caller with READ access to a Submodel can therefore read fields that the access rules hide from them, for example `supplementalSemanticIds` keys that name the other parties allowed to read the Submodel.



If versioning is enabled (`history.mode` set to `api` or `audit`), `GET /submodels/{submodelIdentifier}/$history` and `GET /shells/{aasIdentifier}/$history` in the Submodel Repository, AAS Repository and AAS Environment return the complete stored version without applying the rule's formula or fragment filters. A caller whose rules grant READ on these routes can read fields that the access rules hide, and Submodels and Asset Administration Shells that the direct read does not return to them at all.



The issue is fixed in Eclipse BaSyx Go Components v1.1.3.

advisories.summary: P-Net before 1.0.4 aborts the Application Relationship of an RPC session when a fragment of a...
advisories.description: P-Net before 1.0.4 aborts the Application Relationship of an RPC session when a fragment of a response has been resent without being acknowledged, without checking that the session has an Application Relationship. A request for an existing Application Relationship that is sent on another activity than its Connect, and gets a fragmented response, is handled on a session without one. If the response is not acknowledged, a NULL pointer is dereferenced and the device crashes. A conformant IO-controller does not send such requests. The attacker must have observed the AR UUID of an established Application Relationship and requires ADJACENT network access.

advisories.summary: P-Net before 1.0.4 does not check the number of MCR request blocks in a Connect request against...
advisories.description: P-Net before 1.0.4 does not check the number of MCR request blocks in a Connect request against the number of multicast communication relations that an Application Relationship has room for (PNET_MAX_MC_CR, 1 by default). Each further block is written past the end of the array, into the rest of the Application Relationship and, with more blocks, into the following one. The written data comes from the request. No established Application Relationship is needed, and the attacker requires ADJACENT network access. Builds with PNET_OPTION_MC_CR disabled are not affected.

advisories.summary: P-Net before 1.0.4 finds the RPC session of a received PDU by its activity UUID only, and a...

advisories.summary: P-Net before 1.0.4 does not check the record data length of an IODWrite request to a non-user...
advisories.description: P-Net before 1.0.4 does not check the record data length of an IODWrite request to a non-user record index against the size of the record block header. The 32-bit length is reduced by the header size before it is passed to the record handlers, so a length smaller than the header underflows and the handlers receive a data length of about 65530. The fixed-size reads of the I&M and PDPort handlers can then read past the end of the session buffer. The result of the write is discarded. The attacker must have an established Application Relationship or be able to send in the context of one, and requires ADJACENT network access.

advisories.summary: P-Net before 1.0.4 releases the Application Relationship of an RPC session, without the abort...
advisories.description: P-Net before 1.0.4 releases the Application Relationship of an RPC session, without the abort procedure, when a fragment of a request has another data representation (endianness) than the first fragment of the call. The application is not told that the Application Relationship is gone, the cyclic data stops, and the resources of the Application Relationship are left referencing a cleared structure. Another host can then connect in its place. A host with ADJACENT network access that has observed the activity UUID of the connection, which is sent in clear in every RPC request, can do this with one PDU.

advisories.summary: The system certificate authority (CA) store in Red Hat products, distributed via ca-certificates...
advisories.description:
The system certificate authority (CA) store in Red Hat products, distributed via ca-certificates RPM packages, included multiple root CA certificates of authorities, which signed intermediate CA certificates with weak private keys issued by the eMudhra certificate authority. A man-in-the-middle attacker could use this flaw to issue certificates for arbitrary host names signed by the weak intermediate CA certificates, which would be considered trusted by a TLS/SSL client using system CA store and cause such clients to connect to malicious sites.

Due to inability to only distrust specific intermediate certificates in all clients using the system CA store, root CA certificates of authorities that signed weak intermediate CA certificates are being removed.

advisories.summary:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xen-netback: defer...
advisories.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xen-netback: defer xenvif_mcast_addr_list_free()

In order for the function to legitimately avoid locking/RCU, it needs to
run after all TX/RX processing has finished/stopped: Lookups happen from
xenvif_start_xmit(), while adds/removes happen from xenvif_tx_action()
(called out of xenvif_poll()).

Move the call out of xenvif_disconnect_data() (the call to the function
from connect()'s error path doesn't require any cleaning up there), and
put it past the synchronization point in backend_disconnect().

This is XSA-527 / CVE-2026-100081.

advisories.summary: A flaw was found in D-Bus. With a privileged Monitoring client attached (for example dbus-monitor...
advisories.description: A flaw was found in D-Bus. With a privileged Monitoring client attached (for example dbus-monitor or busctl monitor), an unprivileged local user can cause dbus-daemon to abort if a driver-originated broadcast such as NameOwnerChanged or ActivatableServicesChanged cannot be delivered to a recipient (for example due to a deny rule or an exceeded outgoing message queue). Driver broadcasts still use serial 0; when delivery fails, composing the monitor error reply asserts reply_serial != 0 and aborts the daemon. This is an incomplete fix for CVE-2023-34969, which only assigned serials for driver messages sent to a single recipient. On the well-known system bus this is a denial of service.

advisories.summary: A flaw was found in BusyBox's udhcpc DHCP client. When processing raw DHCP packets, the client...
advisories.description: A flaw was found in BusyBox's udhcpc DHCP client. When processing raw DHCP packets, the client replaces the validated packet length with an attacker-controlled value from the IP header without re-validating the minimum size. This leads to an integer underflow when subtracting header sizes, causing a subsequent memory copy with a massively oversized length. An attacker on the same network segment can send a specially crafted packet to crash the DHCP client, resulting in denial of service and loss of network connectivity.

advisories.summary: In FRRouting 8.4 and later, bgpd frees the same memory twice when dynamic BGP neighbors...
advisories.description: In FRRouting 8.4 and later, bgpd frees the same memory twice when dynamic BGP neighbors disconnect, if the peer-group used by a "bgp listen range" also has a Site-of-Origin configured ("neighbor PG soo"). Each dynamic neighbor shares the peer-group's SoO value instead of getting its own copy, but frees it as its own when the neighbor is deleted, which happens as soon as its connection closes. The first disconnect leaves the peer-group pointing at freed memory, and the second disconnect frees it again, causing bgpd to abort and drop all BGP sessions on the router. Any host whose address falls inside the listen range can trigger this by opening and closing two TCP connections to the BGP port, without sending any BGP message and without knowing the AS number, and can repeat it each time bgpd restarts. If the peer-group has a TCP-MD5 password, only hosts that know the password can trigger it. Two ordinary flaps of legitimate dynamic neighbors have the same effect. Between the two frees, displaying the configuration ("show running-config") or establishing a dynamic neighbor also reads the freed memory, which can crash bgpd after a single disconnect. Only configurations that combine a listen range with a SoO on the same peer-group are affected.

advisories.description:
This vulnerability exists in the eMudhra emBridge due to missing authorization checks in the FileBrowser API endpoints. These endpoints perform file system enumeration using the LocalSystem account without adequately validating the requesting caller's authorization. An unauthenticated attacker on the same LAN could exploit this vulnerability by sending malicious webpage to the local HTTPS Web API.

 

Successful exploitation of this vulnerability could allow the attacker to enumerate file and directory names and obtain information about the directory structure of the targeted system. 



The vulnerability however, does not provide access to file contents or permit file modification, deletion, or code execution, or access to cryptographic keys and hardware token PINs.

advisories.description: Cudy TR3000 before 2.5.42 contains a remote code execution vulnerability that allows unauthenticated adjacent attackers to run root commands by advertising a rogue automesh controller over mDNS. advisories.description: ExcelJS through 4.4.0 contains a memory exhaustion vulnerability in Worksheet._parseMergeCells that allows attackers to crash applications by supplying unbounded mergeCell ranges. Because Contao\User::isEqualTo() and serialized session data omit two-factor state, attackers already holding a session keep it after the owner changes 2FA settings.

advisories.description: OpenMage magento-lts before 20.18.2 and 21.0.0-beta1 before 21.0.0-beta3 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability because storefront MSRP/MAP popup and Qty Increments notice templates output product names without proper escaping. advisories.description: Miniflux before 2.3.5 contains an insufficient session expiration vulnerability that allows attackers to retain account access because password changes do not revoke existing web sessions. advisories.description: OpenMage magento-lts 20.17.0 before 20.18.2 and 21.0.0-beta1 before 21.0.0-beta3 contains an unrestricted file upload vulnerability because the general/file/protected_extensions blocklist omits phar, php8, and phps. advisories.summary: ExcelJS through 4.4.0 contains a memory exhaustion vulnerability that allows attackers to crash...

advisories.description: OpenMage magento-lts before 20.18.2 and 21.0.0-beta1 before 21.0.0-beta3 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in its error pages, which print SCRIPT_NAME-derived URLs built by errors/processor.php without escaping. advisories.summary: The SureDash – Community, Courses & Member Dashboard plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to...
advisories.description: The SureDash – Community, Courses & Member Dashboard plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in all versions up to, and including, 1.13.0 This is due to the `save_settings()` REST handler at `/suredash/v1/save-settings` being gated only by `admin_permission_callback()`, which authorizes any holder of the custom `manage_portal_dashboard` capability (Portal Manager role) without requiring `promote_users`, `edit_users`, or `manage_options`, combined with `sanitize_settings_data()` iterating all attacker-supplied keys with no allow-list, allowing arbitrary keys such as `default_role` to pass through `sanitize_text_field()` unchanged and be persisted into the `portal_settings` option via `update_option()` with no role-validity check. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers with Portal Manager-level access and above to poison the `default_role` setting to `administrator`, after which any subsequent new-user registration through the publicly accessible block-register endpoint reads the corrupted setting and passes it directly to `wp_insert_user()`, producing a full WordPress Administrator account under the attacker's control. The exploit requires two steps: a POST to the authenticated `save-settings` endpoint to overwrite `default_role`, followed by triggering a new registration through the unauthenticated block-register endpoint to receive the escalated account. Successful exploitation causes the attacker's own account to receive the complete administrator role.

advisories.description: The Easy Property Listings plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to generic SQL Injection via the 'post_type' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.5.28 due to insufficient escaping on the user supplied parameter and lack of sufficient preparation on the existing SQL query. advisories.summary: The Chatterbug Forms – Fast, Flexible WordPress Form Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable...
advisories.description: The Chatterbug Forms – Fast, Flexible WordPress Form Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Upload in all versions up to, and including, 1.0.2 via the cbforms_check_form_submissions function. This is due to missing server-side file extension validation in cbforms_check_form_submissions(), where the allowed-type check defaults to the uploaded file's own extension when no field restriction is configured, trivially allowing any extension including .php. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to upload files that may be executable, which makes remote code execution possible. The submission nonce printed inline on every public page containing a Chatterbug form is freely obtainable by unauthenticated visitors and therefore does not constitute an effective access control barrier.

advisories.summary: The Widget Options – Advanced Conditional Visibility for Gutenberg Blocks & Classic Widgets...
advisories.description: The Widget Options – Advanced Conditional Visibility for Gutenberg Blocks & Classic Widgets plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Code Injection in all versions up to, and including, 4.2.6.1 via the `post_content` parameter. This is due to asymmetric parsing between the save-time strip filter (`widgetopts_strip_logic_from_blocks()`) and the render-time parser (`blockopts_filter_before_display()`): embedding an inner `<!--start_widgetopts` literal inside a JSON key causes the write-side `json_decode` to see a non-`class` key and skip stripping — persisting the payload verbatim to the database — while the render-side `str_replace` reconstitutes the key to `class`, feeding the attacker-controlled `logic` value directly into `@eval`. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Author-level access and above, to inject PHP expressions that execute on every front-end page view, enabling boolean-oracle exfiltration of WordPress site configuration data — including admin email address, default role, and arbitrary `get_option`, `get_user_meta`, and `get_post_meta` values — via the plugin's allowlisted-function sandbox, which escalates to unrestricted code execution if any installed plugin extends the `widgetopts_allowed_php_functions` filter. Contributors can also exploit this vulnerability when their submitted post is later published by an administrator; notably, the injected payload executes for all site visitors, including unauthenticated users, because a trust-flag mechanism introduced in version 4.2.6 causes `widgetopts_safe_eval_trusted()` to bypass its non-admin short-circuit at every legacy render callsite. Exploitation by attackers with contributor-level access and above requires that an administrator (or editor) later publishes the contributor's submission. On a default installation, where that is not configured, the vulnerability requires attackers with author-level access and above.

advisories.summary: The WP STAGING – Backups & Restore, Migration & Clone Plugin – Cloud Backups, Scheduled Backups...
advisories.description: The WP STAGING – Backups & Restore, Migration & Clone Plugin – Cloud Backups, Scheduled Backups plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary Directory Deletion in all versions up to, and including, 4.19.0. This is due to insufficient path validation in the `cleanStagingDirectory` function, where the `deleteDir` parameter is only stripped of whitespace and double slashes by `sanitizePath()` without removing `..` traversal sequences or enforcing containment within the staging directory, leaving the sole pre-deletion guard as a simple string equality check against the WordPress home path. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with administrator-level access and above, to recursively delete arbitrary directories on the server — including `wp-content`, `wp-admin`, or directories outside the WordPress installation on shared hosting — resulting in denial of service or permanent data loss. An attacker must sequence a clone start, cancellation, and restart to drive the `delete_job` cache into the `directory` step before re-cancelling with a manipulated `deleteDir` value supplied via the `wp_ajax_wpstg_cancel_clone` endpoint.

advisories.summary: The MISP Modules website component contains an open redirect vulnerability in its login endpoint....
advisories.description: The MISP Modules website component contains an open redirect vulnerability in its login endpoint. The /login route accepted a user-supplied next query parameter and passed it directly to Flask's redirect() function without validating the destination. An attacker could craft a URL such as https://victim-host/login?next=https://attacker.example/phish and deliver it to a user (e.g., via email or a lookalike page). After the user successfully authenticated, the application issued a 302 redirect to the attacker-controlled external URL. This enables phishing attacks where a user, believing they are still on the legitimate MISP Modules site, may enter additional credentials or sensitive information on the attacker's page. It can also be used to obscure the true destination of a link, bypassing user trust in the legitimate domain. The vulnerability requires the victim to interact with the crafted URL and complete a login, but no prior authentication or special configuration is needed on the attacker's side. The affected component is the website sub-project of misp-modules, specifically the account blueprint in website/app/account/account.py. No version boundaries are specified in the patch metadata.

This issue was fixed in version 5.10.2607.  Hotfixes for older versions (5.8) have also been released.

advisories.summary: A flaw was found in Kroxylicious. The ACL authorizer's rules-file parser unquotes `matching /…/`...
advisories.description: A flaw was found in Kroxylicious. The ACL authorizer's rules-file parser unquotes `matching /…/` regular-expression literals using the string unquoting rules, which strips every backslash escape. As a result, an allow rule such as `matching /orders\.v1/` is compiled as the regex `orders.v1`, which also matches unintended names such as `ordersXv1`, and character classes such as `\d` and `\w` lose their special meaning. Allow rules written with regex escapes can therefore apply to more resources than the author intended. Depending on the ACL configuration, this may allow an authenticated Kafka client to access a resource (such as read or write a topic) that should have been denied.

advisories.description:
## Source: kam193 (15bab830cd8343859ac220ef87e821719169a4e2ccb50da37032d97ef02c27dd)
During installation, the package downloads and executes a script from a remote location. The server delivers different payload versions, some of them being benign, and others containing next-stage installation. The final payload is a RAT.


---

Category: MALICIOUS - The campaign has clearly malicious intent, like infostealers.


Campaign: 2026-11-testing1345


Reasons (based on the campaign):


 - Downloads and executes a remote malicious script.


 - The package overrides the install command in setup.py to execute malicious code during installation.


 - rat

---
